Hollis Wend, Warden of the Gate

Welcome to the Labyrinth, traveller. The court is safe; past the gate, nothing is. The stones move every twelve minutes, the hedges every two. Nobody I know has found the Heart, and I have looked for forty years. Keep your wits, and keep going.
Old Tamsin, Keeper of the Clock
You made it! Sit, sit. The clock says you're in good time. Touch the cup when you're ready: it's yours to claim.
The Artificer's echo
Another visitor. The maze let you in, then. It does what it likes these days. What do you want with my workshop?
Querra, the Riddle-Keeper
Few come this way. Answer me, and I will tell you where the Heart's way down lies, for now. Answer wrongly, and the green carries you away.
I have keys but open no locks; I have space but no room; you can enter, but never go inside. What am I?
The more of me you take, the more you leave behind. What am I?
I am always ahead of you, and you will never reach me, though you walk all your life toward me. What am I?

I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish. What am I?
A painting of the sea
What goes through every door in a house, yet never comes in and never goes out?
What can fill a whole room and still take up no space at all?
Break me and I am better than before; keep me and I am useless. What am I?
A record (to be broken)
I turn once, and what is out is not getting in; I turn again, and what is in is not getting out. What am I?
I can be cracked, made, told and played. What am I?
The one who makes me does not need me; the one who buys me does not use me; the one who uses me never knows. What am I?
What has a neck but no head, two arms but no hands?
Walk me forward and I am a path; walk me back and I am a way home. Lose me and you are lost. What am I?
Two doors, two stone guards. One door leads on toward the Heart; the other drops you into the Deep. One guard always tells the truth; the other always lies. You may ask one of them one question.

The Lookout. The hands lift you up the needle of stone and set you down at the top. The whole Labyrinth lies below: stone and hedge tangled together to every horizon, and nowhere any sign of the Heart. By the time you are down again, it will all have moved.
Down. The hands pass you down, hand to hand, into the dark, and let go. You land softly in the Oubliette, in the Deep.

🌀 The ground shudders. All round you the stones of the maze grind and slide into new places, through the hedge and under it. Nothing is where it was.
🌿 A sound like wind in leaves. The hedges are moving: they grow across one path and draw back from another, round the stones and between them.
🌿 You hear leaves rustle behind you. When you look, the way you came has closed .
The wall grows where you stood and moves you gently aside .
Click. The planks tip under you. You slide down a long stone chute into the dark and land, unhurt, in the Oubliette , deep under the maze.
🤢 The Reekmire. You are knee-deep in it, and the smell is beyond anything. Get back on the stones.

✨ The Heart of the Labyrinth. You found it, at the very bottom of everything, far under the Deep. A great hollow under a vault of still lights: fountains, a great clock with thirteen hours, and on its dais the Lantern Cup, glowing. Hardly anyone has ever stood here.

The Labyrinth: the Deep. The stone behind the Maker's Mark swings shut. You are in the Stair of the Mark, under the great maze, among rooms from every age whose doors will not stay as they are. It is Deadly here. The stair goes up to the Gatehouse Court.

The Labyrinth. The court is a clearing in a maze that fills the whole world and never holds still: old stone that rearranges every twelve minutes, and living hedge grown all through it that moves every two. Through the great gate and the court's side arches it goes on for ever. Somewhere, they say, is the Heart, though not where anyone expects. The court is safe. Past its gate and arches, nothing is.
